text:
Maya: Heads-up from the field: two customers asked for a 'priority lane' add-on that guarantees short bursts of extra throughput (up to 2x) for scheduled windows. They want this priced as an add-on to tiers. Thoughts?
Tom: Need to define modes. Two obvious ones: 1) scheduled best-effort (no SLA) 2) scheduled guaranteed (with reserved capacity + SLA).
Elena: Agreed. Also need clear gating on who can buy guaranteed. Reserved capacity means a minimum commit or a seat-based reservation.
Ravi: From infra: guaranteed requires placement reservations and bumping isolation. We can do N extra GPUs during the window but it adds fragmentation ops-side. Auto fallback to best-effort is required.
Maya: What about pricing shapes? Flat monthly fee vs commit-backed holiday pricing?
FinOps: Quick sketch:
- soft-priority: +10% on usage rates, no commit, no credits
- hard-priority: base reservation fee (covers idle cost) + usage multiplier x1.05, 3-month min
Tom: We should allow per-window credit rules. If we miss guaranteed throughput we give a credit tied to that window, not the whole month. Legal will want an explicit remedy.
legal-bot: Draft clause suggestion:```
Priority Lane (Guaranteed)
Provider will provision reserved capacity for Customer during Customer-specified daily windows. Customer must provide windows at least 14 days in advance and may change windows twice per month. If Provider fails to meet committed throughput for a scheduled window, Provider will credit Customer an amount equal to the lesser of (a) 20% of the fee attributable to that window, or (b) actual fees paid for impacted requests. Provider may suspend guaranteed service for force majeure events; credits apply. After 2 missed guaranteed windows in any rolling 90-day period, Customer may terminate the add-on with pro-rata refund for unused reservation period.
```
Elena: Implementation checklist: 1) schedule API + UI (per-customer calendar) 2) placement reservations and reservation allocator 3) metrics: window-level throughput, p50/p95/p99, cold-start events 4) billing line items per-window
Ravi: Tech constraint: instant 2x is expensive. Recommend we support two burst profiles: "fast-burst" (warm-hot extra capacity, 1-2s ramp) and "bulk-burst" (slower spin-up, 10-60s). Expose to customers.
Maya: For pilots, propose: offer soft-priority trial to any customer for 30 days; hard-priority pilots require a PO and a 3-month minimum.
Tom: Launch criteria proposal: (a) console scheduling + API live, (b) 2 hard-priority pilots or 6 soft-priority pilots, (c) billing + invoice line per-window verified, (d) legal signoff on SLA language, (e) perf: p99 within SLA for 95% of windows in staging stress tests.
FinOps: Need unit economics doc before pilot: simulate idle cost, expected utilization, and churn risk. I can run sims if product picks baseline #s.
Maya: For sales negotiation playbook: when customer asks for trial hard-guarantee, insist on soft-trial first; accept exceptions only with RevOps+FinOps signoff.
legal-bot: Also add change-notice window: customers can change schedule with 72h notice, last-minute changes by customer accepted but may be subject to non-guaranteed performance.
Ravi: Operationally: add auto-fallback that routes to default models or soft-priority and flags ticket to oncall. When fallback occurs auto-credit calculation should run.
Elena: UX: console should show upcoming scheduled windows, expected reserved capacity, and a simple "cost estimator" for chosen windows.
Maya: Next steps: @FinOps run econ sims (due Wed), @Ravi prototype allocator ETA 2 weeks, @Tom draft pilot offer email, @legal-bot expand clause with termination language, @Elena mock Console flows. Check-in Fri 10am. :calendar:
